proposition: From the current state estimate, an N-step lookahead tree searches for a control whose every possible observation trajectory reaches a diagnosable state before the boundary; active N-diagnosability is a conservative sufficient condition for active diagnosability.
quality_notes: Direct prior art for online finite-lookahead active diagnosis; untimed state-output model

proposition: Algorithm 1 either returns a diagnostic control sequence from the current estimate or establishes failure within the chosen lookahead; its complexity is O(N times the controlled-observation alphabet size to the power 2N).

proposition: State estimates are recursively updated from the full sequence of enforced controls and observed outputs; a diagnostic control must work and remain executable for every compatible trajectory from the current estimate.
quality_notes: Strong prior art for history-compatible candidate sets and universal action feasibility; timing uncertainty is outside the reviewed model.

proposition: An observer construction checks active diagnosability and returns a feasible diagnostic control, with a double-exponential worst-case state bound.
quality_notes: Computational result concerns full control-sequence synthesis rather than one-step minimax selection

locator: pp. 1897-1898; Section III battery model and conclusion
proposition: The application composes a 6561-state four-battery DES and derives a four-step charging/discharging diagnostic control for two modeled temperature outputs.
quality_notes: This is a model-based illustration; the reviewed article reports no physical execution, sample size, measurement data, uncertainty analysis, or comparative accuracy.

locator: p. 537 (PDF p. 11), Theorem 31; p. 538 (PDF p. 12), Section 5 and reference [7]
proposition: The conference paper gives a waiting-time optimization result; Section 5 points to Research Report LSV-13-12 (2013) for the detailed parameterized-permissiveness treatment.

proposition: Algorithm 3 performs the online synthesis step from the current estimate by choosing event disablement or a time-interval restriction.
quality_notes: Algorithmic locator separated from the supervisor and state-estimate definitions in EVID-2026-014.

locator: Crossref publisher-registered abstract and bibliographic metadata; Fränzle et al. 2026 Article 17 p. 5 and reference [24] on p. 31
proposition: The abstract reports an online incremental diagnosis algorithm with bounded worst-case diagnostic delay whenever diagnosis is possible. Separately, it reports a practical sound but not necessarily complete procedure whose computation time and space are bounded by system-model size and do not depend on the number of observations.
quality_notes: No full article was obtained. The exact relation between the two reported results, their premises, state update, intervention, stopping semantics, artifact evaluation, and comparison with CL-TAV remain unverified; this evidence is contextual only.

locator: pp. 2-3; passive diagnosis statement and contribution
proposition: The method diagnoses faults by passively and centrally observing system behavior, for example by listening to network messages, and is designed not to add load or otherwise interfere with the system.
quality_notes: This is passive diagnosis, not active testing or adaptive intervention selection; it therefore does not subsume CL-TAV C2.

proposition: The formal guarantees assume separate system and diagnoser clocks (A1), an observable/unobservable action partition (A2), exact-once observation of every observable event and no spurious observation (A3), that every finite run can be continued so its continuation contains an observable (A4), a timed-automaton system model (A5), bounded action-specific latency (A6), and clock drift/offset represented by a slope-bounded time-remapping function.
quality_notes: A3 excludes missing, duplicate, and spurious observations. A4's stated existential-continuation wording and its later use for Algorithm 1 termination are separated in EVID-2026-052. None of A1-A6 transfers automatically to CL-TAV.

locator: Definition 3.2 p. 10; Definition 3.4 p. 11; pp. 11-14, equations (8)-(10)
proposition: Consistency pairs each observation bijectively with a same-action event whose occurrence lies in its latency-and-clock-adjusted interval. Online diagnosis ranges over every run that can produce the observed time projection plus possible late arrivals; a fault is reported only when every such run contains it.
quality_notes: This is strong prior art for compatible-history possible-run semantics under observation-time uncertainty, but its exact-once observation and timed-automaton assumptions delimit transfer.

locator: equation (10) p. 13; equation (12) p. 14; Theorems 4.3-4.4 pp. 16-17; Theorem 4.6 and Corollary 4.7 pp. 17-18; Theorem 4.9 pp. 18 and 40-47; Theorem 4.12 p. 20
proposition: The active-prefix decision criterion is sound and Delta-complete with Delta=(1+epsilon)(max latency upper bound minus min latency lower bound): if the observations available at time t already make the fault necessary, then for every possible continuation and every t' greater than t+Delta the diagnoser reports it on every t'-projection. Consistency is equivalent to finite difference-bound consistency, and the finite-observation diagnosis question is decidable by timed-automata reachability.
quality_notes: Here 'active prefix' is an observation subset, not an actively chosen test. Delta is an additional diagnosis offset after the Eq. (10) necessity condition holds; it is not an unconditional fault-occurrence-to-alarm bound, computation time, or evidence that a CL-TAV execution met E-TIME.

proposition: The exact online algorithm incrementally maintains observation prefixes and diagnosis states containing an abstract timed-system zone, matched observations, and occurred faults; it adds timing-difference constraints for each observation and is sound and Delta-complete in the Eq. (10) sense, but its time and space grow with the number of observations.
quality_notes: The conditional scope of Delta-completeness is stated in EVID-2026-043. This is a passive compatible-history mechanism; it neither selects interventions nor implements CL-TAV's versioned no-resurrection interface.

proposition: Retaining at most B observations' timing-difference history yields an over-approximating diagnoser that remains sound but is not generally Delta-complete. It uses at most B additional clocks; for fixed B, insertion time and space are bounded by model size and independent of observation count, with polynomial rank B in the original model size.
quality_notes: The resource bound is for the approximate bounded-history variant. It must not be attributed to the exact algorithm, and any CL-TAV history truncation would require its own explicit guarantee.

proposition: The prototype case study uses simulated traces from a configurable sorting-conveyor timed-automata family, a JANI/Momba implementation with DBMs and depth-first exploration, one 2.2 GHz Xeon core and 4 GB RAM, and 1000 simulated 120-second runs per configuration.
quality_notes: The authors call this a first case study and state that thorough empirical evaluation is out of scope; it is not physical or aerospace evidence.

proposition: In the reported model family, bounded history sharply reduces per-observation runtime but can delay or eliminate diagnosability; unbounded-history median processing rose from 0.05 s in the second quarter to 1.87 s in the last quarter, while B=5 remained 0.027 s in both. The high-jitter Figure 11(c) configuration creates many possible observation orderings, increases per-observation runtime, and can mask timing-based faults.
quality_notes: These are model-specific simulation results without a CL-TAV comparator. The paper's separate high-latency interpretation and an Eq. (12) recomputation are isolated in EVID-2026-050 and EVID-2026-051 rather than treated as this DIRECT experimental result.

locator: p. 13 online-diagnoser definition; pp. 30-32 diagnosability discussion and conclusion
proposition: The diagnoser returns the set of faults that must have occurred; when a fault is observationally indistinguishable it is simply not diagnosed. The reviewed formalism defines neither an intervention policy nor CL-TAV-style exclusive stopping, budget, abstention, recovery, or error outcomes.
quality_notes: This carefully delimits the output semantics: non-diagnosis is not the same construct as a registered stop or abstention decision.

proposition: The paper identifies a reference implementation in Momba, conveyor-belt models and experiments, and a Zenodo artifact for reproducing the reported case study.
quality_notes: Artifact availability improves reproducibility of the source study but does not make it a task-equivalent or authorized CL-TAV experimental baseline.

proposition: The authors state that high latency in Figure 11(b) is not itself a runtime problem and mostly pertains to the diagnosis offset Delta, described there as the time until an observation becomes settled and must be considered for diagnosis.
quality_notes: This records the authors' explanation, not an endorsed causal inference. Its relation to Eq. (12) is unresolved because configurations (a) [1,3] ms and (b) [2999,3001] ms have the same 2 ms span under the shared epsilon=0.01 and therefore yield the same formula value when the interval applies uniformly to the relevant observables.

locator: equation (12) p. 14; Section 6 model parameter p. 27; Figure 11 and Section 6.3 p. 31
proposition: Reviewer recomputation under the stated epsilon=0.01 and the condition that each Figure 11 latency interval applies uniformly to the relevant observable actions gives Delta=2.02 ms for (a) [1,3] ms, Delta=2.02 ms for (b) [2999,3001] ms, and Delta=2020 ms for (c) [1000,3000] ms. Uniformly translating every action's latency interval leaves max l_max minus min l_min unchanged; changing only some actions can change it.
quality_notes: This is algebraic review, not a new experiment or an author-reported result. It exposes a surface ambiguity with the p. 31 explanation without declaring the paper or its theorem incorrect, and it supplies no CL-TAV timing guarantee.

locator: assumption A4 p. 4; Algorithm 1 termination explanation p. 23
proposition: A4 is stated as every finite run having a continuation that contains an observable; the Algorithm 1 termination paragraph invokes A4 as meaning there can be no cycles free of observables. The equivalence of these formulations is not established in the reviewed passages, because an observable-free cycle may still have an observable exit.
quality_notes: This is a quantifier/premise clarification, not a completed counterexample or a finding that the full method is invalid. CL-TAV does not inherit A4; its own budget, round, retry, and termination resources remain governed by project contracts.

locator: printed p. 55/PDF p. 1, Introduction and Fig. 1

quality_notes: IMA/ARINC 653 context, not ARINC 615A data loading. It supports configuration-aware test boundaries but not a CL-TAV result or novelty claim.

proposition: The proposed workflow derives timed test stimuli and oracles from behavioral models, generates TTCN-3 procedures, and executes hardware/software integration tests at hardware interfaces; its example explicitly models environment nondeterminism and response delays.
quality_notes: This is an avionics test-automation precedent. Its offline path resolution and IMA interface tests are not equivalent to CL-TAV online residual-set selection.

locator: printed pp. 61–62/PDF pp. 7–8, §III Estimation of Efficiency Gain and §IV conclusion
proposition: The authors estimate that model-based testing would require about 40% of traditional testing effort when suitable test models already exist and less than 80% when models must be created; these are remaining-workload ratios based on experience and other domains, not measured savings from a controlled study in this paper.
quality_notes: Do not invert the 40%–80% remaining-workload interval into a quoted savings result, cite it as observed avionics productivity, or use it to forecast CL-TAV savings.

locator: printed p. 62/PDF p. 8, Conclusions and future work

quality_notes: The paper cannot serve as executed ARINC 653 conformance evidence, still less as ARINC 615A conformance evidence.

locator: printed pp. 67-68/PDF pp. 1-2, Abstract and Introduction
proposition: The authors describe repeated manual simulator scenarios and visual checking as a laborious industrial practice, then propose an ARINC 661 model-, constraint-, simulator-, OCR-, and image-processing-based automated test workflow for a primary flight display.
quality_notes: Useful avionics workflow context only. Display correctness and ARINC 661 differ from data-loader protocol confirmation under ARINC 615A.

locator: printed pp. 74-75/PDF pp. 8-9, Tables II-IV and Evaluation
proposition: The industrial case used a 14-state, 24-guard, 33-transition model with 30 constraints; 494 paths were generated, 34 paths were selected to cover important states, producing 34 JSBSim scripts, 30133 instance models, and 1800 minutes of evaluated images.

locator: printed pp. 75-76/PDF pp. 9-10, Evaluation and Limitations
proposition: The paper reports 18 identified faults, while its result discussion attributes 13 to functionality absent from the simulator and reflected in constraints; three major PFD faults are separately described.
quality_notes: The source's labels are retained. This is adverse evidence that model, simulator, oracle, and implementation discrepancy classes must be separated before a localization count is interpreted as independent product defects.

proposition: The approach requires preparation of test-ready behavioral models and OCL constraints, and OCR accuracy is not perfect; the authors use segmentation and image preprocessing to mitigate the latter.
quality_notes: Preparation and oracle instrumentation costs belong in an end-to-end comparison rather than being silently excluded from action or setup cost.

proposition: Selective prediction permits a model to predict or abstain; coverage is the probability mass of the accepted region, selective risk is loss conditional on acceptance, and a risk-coverage curve relates the two.
quality_notes: Cross-domain evaluation concept only. It supports reporting attempt coverage separately from answered-case error and does not validate SelectiveNet, its loss, or its guarantees for CL-TAV.

proposition: The paper distinguishes requested target coverage from realized coverage and uses an independent validation set to calibrate the selection threshold.
quality_notes: CL-TAV does not inherit the paper's statistical assumptions. The transferable caution is only that a declared abstention target is not itself an observed coverage result.

proposition: For randomized algorithms, the paper argues that performance observations require independent runs and that reporting averages alone can conceal distributional differences.
quality_notes: Applies only when the implementation, data generation, injection, or ordering is stochastic. It does not require repeated seeds for a fully deterministic comparison by itself.

proposition: The guidance separates dichotomous success probability from successful-run time, treats time-limit observations as right-censored, and recommends nonparametric tests plus effect sizes such as Vargha-Delaney A12 or odds ratios rather than significance alone.
quality_notes: The paper also notes that embedded and hardware-in-the-loop experiments may be expensive; its large-run examples are not a universal CL-TAV sample-size prescription. Experimental units and dependence still require domain-specific registration.

proposition: The paper recommends publishing raw results, reporting effect sizes with statistical tests, and choosing procedures that match the data and question rather than applying a single default test.
quality_notes: This supports transparent reporting only for applicable randomized comparisons; it does not select a CL-TAV baseline or authorize an experiment.

locator: publisher and author-group abstract; IEEE AES Magazine 36(5):38-47
proposition: The abstract states that loadable-airborne-system characteristics had not been systematically organized in prior literature and that industry lacked an organized set of reusable requirements and tests; the paper proposes a framework for those systems.
quality_notes: Historical abstract-stage record. The authors' absence claim remains unverified; full-text framework, survey, test-structure, and limitation evidence is now separated in EVID-2026-067 through EVID-2026-070.

locator: printed pp. 40-41/PDF pp. 3-4, Surveys and Figures 1-2
proposition: The paper surveyed 20 system developers, 15 with more than ten years of aviation experience, and 12 maintenance technicians, eight with more than ten years of experience. Reported findings include unanimous agreement on integrity importance and framework usefulness, 95% agreement on identity importance, and author-coded concerns about incomplete loading and version conflict.
quality_notes: Descriptive practitioner surveys with small purposive domain samples; the paper groups neutral with agreement for Survey 1 findings and reports no inferential statistics. These responses do not validate the framework's effectiveness.

locator: printed pp. 41-45/PDF pp. 4-8, F-LAS Framework; Figures 3-8; Table 1
proposition: F-LAS defines actors, software distribution, 23 reusable requirements in basic loading, manual check, automatic check, and version-exchange groups, plus six procedures spanning normal loading, interrupted/incomplete loading, and conflicting software versions under manual or automatic checking; Table 1 traces every requirement to at least one procedure.
quality_notes: This is the source's proposed framework and traceability structure, not evidence that the procedures were executed or that they cover ARINC 615A protocol obligations. ARINC 666/667 and DO-178C/DO-326A context must not be promoted to protocol authority.

locator: printed p. 46/PDF p. 9, Conclusion and future work
proposition: The authors list formal feedback from the original survey respondents, compatibility analysis extension, and validation with ARINC 666/667-2 working-group participants as future work; the article reports no execution of the six test procedures and no measured detection or conformance outcome.
quality_notes: The framework supports problem framing and candidate scenario design only. It does not establish effectiveness, certification acceptance, ARINC 615A conformance, or a CL-TAV baseline result.

proposition: The printed ACR-17 sentence calls for a confirmation message when the loaded version is not correct, while ACR-15 calls for confirmation when it is correct and the surrounding error-handling structure distinguishes success from incomplete-load error. The intended ACR-17 message type is therefore textually ambiguous.
quality_notes: Source-internal wording issue only. Do not silently correct or import ACR-17; any use requires human interpretation against the authoritative standards and project requirements.

proposition: The journal article explicitly extends the 2019 conference work by expanding the ARINC 661 profile and tool compatibility, improving image segmentation and evaluation to reduce false positives and comparisons, and adding a second industrial GCS-CDS case study.
quality_notes: Version-specific extension relationship is explicit. Conference and journal counts must remain tied to their respective versions rather than merged.

locator: printed pp. 1995-1997/PDF pp. 19-21, Sections 6.4-6.5 and Tables 1-3
proposition: The evaluation generated 494 PFD paths and selected 34 using stated end-to-end, turn, loop, and state-coverage criteria; it generated 1460 GCS-CDS paths and selected 64 by the same criteria. The source reports 30133 PFD images with 990 failed constraints, one false positive, and 17 unique constraint-level faults grouped into three major types, plus 32910 GCS-CDS images with 20632 failed constraints, eight false positives, and 25 unique constraint-level faults grouped into four major types.
quality_notes: The selected paths were not sampled randomly, images are repeated observations inside paths, and constraint-level unique faults are further grouped into fault types. None of these counts is an independent CL-TAV trial denominator.

locator: printed pp. 1996 and 1999/PDF pp. 20 and 23, RQ2 and Section 6.5.2
proposition: For precision, the study logs simulator data at one-second intervals, populates comparator instance models with those data, applies the same OCL constraints, and matches simulator-data results to image-derived results; it reports mean per-state precision of approximately 99.80% for PFD and 99.62% for GCS-CDS.
quality_notes: The reported precision concerns the OCR/image path relative to simulator-data evaluation with shared constraints. It is not independent injected-fault truth, localization accuracy, recall, or an end-to-end safety/conformance measure.

proposition: The authors limit generalization beyond the two industrial cases and identify instrumentation errors in state machines, OCL constraints, and simulator scripts, experimenter bias, computer-vision accuracy, model-preparation effort, and OCR limitations; domain experts reviewed the input artifacts and public artifacts/datasets are reported.
quality_notes: Domain-expert review and artifact availability mitigate but do not eliminate common-model or common-oracle dependence. The paper remains a different avionics task and is not a fair executable CL-TAV arm.

locator: review inference from printed pp. 1996-2000/PDF pp. 20-24
proposition: Because the image-derived verdict and simulator-data comparator share the same OCL constraints, the reported precision primarily estimates observation-extraction false positives conditional on that oracle; it cannot independently establish that the constraints or simulator encode correct avionics behavior.
quality_notes: Reviewer inference, not an author claim. It motivates independent truth and oracle-diversity checks for CL-TAV without declaring the source evaluation invalid.

proposition: The survey defines mutation score as killed mutants divided by total non-equivalent mutants, explains that complete automatic equivalent-mutant detection is impossible in general because program equivalence is undecidable, and identifies equivalence classification and oracle checking as human-effort costs.
quality_notes: Directly supports excluding confirmed equivalent mutants from the mutation-score denominator while retaining and reporting them as experiment outcomes. It does not define how CL-TAV protocol mutants are proven equivalent.

proposition: The survey reports earlier empirical studies in which 10-40% of mutants were equivalent and reviews compiler, constraint, slicing, co-evolution, and execution-impact techniques for assisting detection.
quality_notes: Historical cross-study range only. It is not a prevalence estimate, prior, sample-size input, or exclusion quota for the CL-TAV fault domain.

proposition: In JAXEN 1.1.1, 9819 mutations were generated; among 1933 covered but not killed mutations, the authors randomly chose 20 from different classes and classified them independently. Ten were non-equivalent, eight equivalent, and two undecided; assessment took 1-50 minutes per mutation and about 15 minutes per mutation per person on average.
quality_notes: Small exploratory sample from one Java program. The explicit undecided category and manual cost are transferable cautions; the 40% value is not transferable to CL-TAV.

proposition: Among 20 highest-impact surviving mutants, 18 were classified non-equivalent and two equivalent; among 20 lowest-impact mutants, nine were non-equivalent and 11 equivalent. Fisher's exact test gave p=0.006, while the authors explicitly warn that impact ranking biases the mutant set and may not represent general test-suite quality.
quality_notes: Impact-based filtering can reduce equivalence review burden but changes the evaluated fault population. It must not be used as an unreported exclusion rule in CL-TAV experiments.

locator: printed pp. 197-198/PDF pp. 6-7, Threats to validity and Conclusion
proposition: The authors state that results from the single JAXEN program are not claimed to generalize, equivalence assessment may contain assessor error or bias, high-impact selection creates construct bias, and the reported approach requires further subjects and assessment.
quality_notes: Supports conservative use of the study: preserve equivalent and undecided categories, report reviewer process, and avoid treating one program's proportions as a protocol-testing constant.
